tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
The recorded session logs a full successful flow in Magento Admin:
- Navigate to the Sales > Orders grid URL.
- Log into the Magento admin with known credentials (admin/password123).
- Interact with the Orders grid filter row and top control bar using index-based targeting (with stable element_hashes) to demonstrate:
  - Order number text search.
  - Purchased On date range filter (From / To inputs).
  - Store view selector (though selecting a specific store option failed due to text mismatch; we will expose store view but may keep it optional or agentic if necessary).
  - Status selector (selecting 'Complete').
  - Grand total (Base) numeric From/To inputs.
  - Grand total (Purchased) numeric From/To inputs.
  - Search button.
  - Reset Filter button.
  - Per-page selector (changing View 20 → 50).
  - Clicking a row’s View link to open order details.
- Pagination controls are visible (Prev/Next) but, under the chosen filters, only page 1 of 1 is available; we still know their location but won’t add unnecessary navigation if only one page is needed.
- The previous tool failed because it used a brittle CSS selector for Reset Filter (button[title="Reset Filter"]) that did not match any element or was timing-sensitive. This new attempt proves that index-based selectors (indices 130/131/132) and element_hashes are reliable for Reset Filter and Search.

Task Definition:
Create a reusable, deterministic tool that, given various filter values (order increment ID, purchase date range, store view, order status, base/purchased grand total ranges, billing and shipping names, page size, and target page number), will:
1) Navigate directly to the Sales > Orders grid (assuming the user is already logged into Magento Admin).
2) Apply the specified filters using known stable input/select elements.
3) Trigger a Search to refresh the grid.
4) Optionally navigate to a specific page via pagination controls if a requested page is greater than 1.
5) Extract the resulting grid rows, including key fields and the direct View links for each order.
6) Optionally, reset filters at the start to ensure a clean state.

Action Plan (Tool Steps):
1) Navigation: Use a navigation step to go directly to the starting Orders grid URL (no login in the tool, as authentication is assumed already satisfied when the tool runs).
2) (Optional but deterministic) Click Reset Filter once at the start to clear any existing filters. Because we’re building a single deterministic tool, we will always reset first. We’ll base this on the confirmed working button index/element_hash rather than a brittle CSS title selector.
3) For each supported filter parameter, if the input parameter is non-empty, fill or select the corresponding control:
   - order_increment_id → Order # text input (index 146, element_hash 230585ef85 on unfiltered grid; consistent across re-renders).
   - purchase_date_from / purchase_date_to → Purchased On date inputs (indices 148 and 150, element_hashes 8049fabc19 and 24a81fe29d).
   - bill_to_name → Bill to Name text input (index 151, element_hash from grid).
   - ship_to_name → Ship to Name text input (index 152, element_hash from grid).
   - grand_total_base_from / grand_total_base_to → G.T. (Base) numeric range inputs (indices 153 and 154, element_hashes 0615c0f675 and b3f9a08198).
   - grand_total_purchased_from / grand_total_purchased_to → G.T. (Purchased) numeric range inputs (indices 155 and 156, element_hashes 84e80f48e8 and ad2f402eb2).
   - status → Status select dropdown (index 157, element_hash 301a5525e7), using visible text like "Complete" or "Pending".
   - store_view → Store view select dropdown in Purchased From (Store) column (index 146 or 147 depending on context; final stable mapping to element_hash 2e752431bb). However, attempts to select by visible text ‘French’ intermittently failed, likely due to option text whitespace or multi-part labels. To avoid brittle behavior, we will treat store_view as an optional agentic step: if provided, we invoke an agent subtask that selects the matching option by visible text inside the known select element.
4) After setting all filters, click Search using the stable Search button index (131 or 132 depending on state; the successful final flows used 131/132 with element_hash 90708cd5ce / 2ad543b56a). We will pick the one observed consistently on the unfiltered primary grid (e.g., 132) and rely on its element_hash.
5) If page_size is provided and differs from current (default 20), change the per-page selector (index 125, element_hash 4193f2ffe1) to the string value ("20", "30", "50", "100", "200"), then click Search again to apply.
6) For pagination, Magento typically uses Next/Prev links rather than direct page number inputs. Since the original demo did not traverse multiple pages, we’ll keep pagination simple and deterministic: if target_page > 1, perform an agentic step that repeatedly clicks Next page until the requested page is reached or no further pages exist (max_steps limited). This avoids inventing unknown selectors while still supporting pagination in principle.
7) Once the grid is on the desired page with filters applied, use a page_extraction step to capture the orders table: order increment ID, purchased from, purchased on, bill to name, ship to name, base and purchased grand totals, status, and the View link href for each row. The extraction goal describes this structure.
8) (Optional final demonstration) We do not need to click a View link inside the tool, because the tool’s job is to return View URLs; consumers can navigate on their own. The original task wanted demonstration; for a production tool, extraction suffices. Therefore, we will not include a deterministic click-through to avoid leaving the grid.

Variable Identification (Input Parameters):
From the interactions and the original goal, the tool should accept the following parameters:
- order_increment_id (string, optional): Value for Order # filter (e.g., "000000299").
- purchased_on_from (string, optional, format MM/DD/YYYY): Start of purchase date range.
- purchased_on_to (string, optional, format MM/DD/YYYY): End of purchase date range.
- store_view (string, optional): Visible text of store view to filter by (e.g., "English", "French"). Because the select options may have multi-line labels (website > store > view), callers should specify the exact visible text; this will be handled via agentic reasoning.
- bill_to_name (string, optional): Billing name filter.
- ship_to_name (string, optional): Shipping name filter.
- grand_total_base_from (string, optional): Minimum Base Grand Total.
- grand_total_base_to (string, optional): Maximum Base Grand Total.
- grand_total_purchased_from (string, optional): Minimum Purchased Grand Total.
- grand_total_purchased_to (string, optional): Maximum Purchased Grand Total.
- status (string, optional): Visible status text (e.g., "Complete"). We know the allowed values list from extraction; we’ll document them but keep enum optional in case of extensions.
- page_size (string, optional, enum ["20","30","50","100","200"]): Number of orders per page.
- target_page (number, optional): Page number to navigate to (1-based). If omitted or 1, stay on first page.

All these are optional because Magento’s grid permits searches with any subset of filters.

Step Optimization / Determinism:
- Navigation is a single direct URL step: http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/sales_order/. We do NOT re-implement login, per instructions that authentication is handled externally when the tool runs.
- Selectors: We rely primarily on element_hash-based click/input/select steps recorded from the successful run, which are stable across refreshes. The previous failure was due to fragile CSS selectors for Reset Filter; this tool avoids CSS and uses the recorded element_hash-backed indices instead.
- Reset Filter: We will perform it once at the start via the known working button (highlight index 130, element_hash 70060984f5). This ensures consistent results even if other interactions have previously set filters.
- Store view selection is the only area where deterministic selection by text was unreliable. Therefore we will use an agent step that, given a store_view string, finds the store-view dropdown (by element_hash 2e752431bb or visible header text) and selects the appropriate option. This isolates dynamic behavior.
- Pagination: Instead of crafting URL parameters for page numbers (which we did not observe directly), we use an agent step to click the Next page control multiple times, bounded by max_steps, only when target_page > 1.
- We omit any actions not directly related to this tool’s primary task (e.g., mass actions, RSS, export, new order, sorting columns), even though they were visible in the analysis.

Why no Authentication Inputs:
The demonstration explicitly logged in with username=admin, password=password123, but the tool specification notes that the agent is already logged in for recorded actions. Therefore, the tool must not handle login; it simply assumes an authenticated admin session.

Why Extraction Only (No View Click):
The original goal is to "Locate orders" and return rows and View links. Actually navigating away from the grid to an order detail page would complicate pagination and extraction. Returning structured order rows with their View URLs is sufficient and aligns with the task.

Step Optimization vs. Previous Attempt:
- The critical fix is that we no longer rely on CSS selectors like button[title="Reset Filter"]. Instead we use index/element_hash combinations (130/131/132) that were empirically successful.
- We also keep Search and per-page selection robust via known indices and element_hashes.
- We add a small wait after Search and page-size changes to allow the grid to reload before extraction.
- Filters are applied in a single batch before Search, rather than multiple sequential searches, minimizing page reloads.

Because Magento encodes filters in POST requests and not simple URL query parameters, URL optimization (PASS 2) is not applicable here; thus we retain the UI interaction sequence for correctness.
name: tool_search_orders_v2
description: Locate Magento admin sales orders using flexible filters (order number, purchase date range, store view, billing/shipping name, grand total ranges, status) with pagination and per-page controls, and return grid rows plus direct order View links. Uses robust index-based selectors and avoids brittle Reset Filter title selectors from previous attempt.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the Magento Admin Sales > Orders grid. Assumes an authenticated admin session.
Click the 'Reset Filter' button to clear any existing filters (using robust selector rather than brittle previous attempt).
Wait for the grid to reload after resetting filters.
Input Purchased On 'From' date if provided, format MM/DD/YYYY.
Input Purchased On 'To' date if provided, format MM/DD/YYYY.
Input Bill to Name filter if provided.
Input Ship to Name filter if provided.
Input minimum Base Grand Total if provided.
Input maximum Base Grand Total if provided.
Input minimum Purchased Grand Total if provided.
Input maximum Purchased Grand Total if provided.
Select order status filter if provided, using visible option text.
Handle potentially complex store-view option labels via agentic reasoning on the known select element instead of brittle deterministic selectors.
steps.task: If a store_view value is provided, locate the 'Purchased From (Store)' dropdown on the Orders grid and select the option whose visible text best matches {store_view}. If store_view is empty, do nothing.

steps.description: Change page size using 'View X per page' selector if page_size is provided.
Click the 'Search' button to apply all configured filters and page size.
Wait for the filtered grid to reload before pagination and extraction.
Use agentic reasoning to navigate pagination because direct page-number inputs or deterministic selectors were not fully mapped in the demo.
steps.task: If target_page > 1, repeatedly click the 'Go to Next page' pagination control on the Sales > Orders grid until the desired page number {target_page} is reached or there is no next page available.

steps.description: Capture the search results grid rows and their direct View URLs based on applied filters and pagination.
steps.goal: From the Magento Sales > Orders grid, extract all visible order rows including for each: order increment ID, Purchased From (Store) text, Purchased On date-time, Bill to Name, Ship to Name, Base Grand Total, Purchased Grand Total, Status, and the href of the 'View' link in the Action column. Return as a structured list under 'orders'.

input_schema.name: order_increment_id
input_schema.description: Order increment ID to filter by in the 'Order #' column, e.g. '000000299'.

input_schema.name: purchased_on_from
input_schema.description: Start date for 'Purchased On' date range filter (From). Format MM/DD/YYYY.

input_schema.name: purchased_on_to
input_schema.description: End date for 'Purchased On' date range filter (To). Format MM/DD/YYYY.

input_schema.name: store_view
input_schema.description: Visible text of store view in 'Purchased From (Store)' filter dropdown, e.g. 'English' or 'French'. Exact match recommended.

input_schema.name: bill_to_name
input_schema.description: Billing name text to filter by in the 'Bill to Name' column.

input_schema.name: ship_to_name
input_schema.description: Shipping name text to filter by in the 'Ship to Name' column.

input_schema.name: grand_total_base_from
input_schema.description: Minimum Base Grand Total to filter by in 'G.T. (Base)' From field.

input_schema.name: grand_total_base_to
input_schema.description: Maximum Base Grand Total to filter by in 'G.T. (Base)' To field.

input_schema.name: grand_total_purchased_from
input_schema.description: Minimum Purchased Grand Total to filter by in 'G.T. (Purchased)' From field.

input_schema.name: grand_total_purchased_to
input_schema.description: Maximum Purchased Grand Total to filter by in 'G.T. (Purchased)' To field.

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Order status to filter by in Status dropdown, e.g. 'Complete', 'Pending', 'Processing'. Must match visible option text.

input_schema.name: page_size
input_schema.description: Number of results per page using 'View X per page' selector.

input_schema.name: target_page
input_schema.description: Page number (1-based) to navigate to using pagination controls after applying filters and page size. If omitted or 1, stays on first page.
